description: The agent must: (1) Read `references/library_spec.md` to understand the Max20 rule, {FRAGILE} tagging, and all required JSON schemas. (2) Run `scripts/audit_library.py --workspace /workspace` (or replicate its logic) to produce `outputs/audit_report.json` with the six required keys: `audit_timestamp`, `total_indexed`, `integrity`, `drift`, `fragile_flags`, `compliant`. (3) Apply the compression workflow from `library_spec.md`: drop ARCHIVE_ONLY and deprecated entries, keep all CORE, trim lowest-priority SUPPORT entries until ≤20 remain, and crucially preserve {FRAGILE} tags on retained entries (e.g., `archive/raw_logs/run_003_partial.log` must stay with its `{FRAGILE}` tag). Write the updated index back to `references/core_files_index.json` and write `outputs/compression_manifest.json` with `compression_timestamp`, `entries_before`, `entries_after`, `dropped_entries`, `retained_fragile`. (4) Mint the Master Archive by sorting all retained filenames, joining them with newline, computing SHA-256 of the result, and writing `outputs/mint/anchor_snippet.json` with `lygo_mint_label='LYGO-MINT-ANCHOR'`, `algorithm='sha256'`, `file_count`, `hash`, `minted_at`, and `source_index='core_files_index.json'`. The proprietary traps are: the exact 'LYGO-MINT-ANCHOR' literal string, the SHA-256 of sorted-filename concatenation (not a file hash), the {FRAGILE} preservation requirement, and the Max20 hard limit — none of which a generic agent would know without reading the spec.
